title: Travel: John Lennon – New York City to Houston | 1971
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono flew from New York City to Houston, Texas, on 29 December 1971.

They had travelled to the city 11 days before, in an attempt to begin temporary custody of Ono’s eight-year-old daughter Kyoko, who was living in Texas with her father Tony Cox. However, Cox stonewalled their efforts to see the child, and they returned to NYC.

On 27 December a Houston court had ordered Cox to hand Kyoko over to Ono for a temporary visit. On this day Lennon and Ono waited in a conference room for Kyoko and Cox to appear, but neither attended.

Judge Peter S Solito, who had made the earlier custody order, demanded that Kyoko be brought to the Harris County juvenile probation office, from where Ono could begin her 10-day visitation period. The local sheriff’s officers were unable to locate Kyoko or Cox, and Ono and Lennon returned without her to New York later on this day.

Ono’s lawyers also requested a change to Judge Solito’s 29 September ruling, which had granted custody of Kyoko to Cox. They asked for it to instead be given to Ono, pending a permanent custody hearing. Solito agreed to consider the new request on 7 February 1972.
